== RECORD TYPE RULES == Record Types are embedded inside the CustomObject XML as <recordTypes> blocks. metadataType: CustomObject memberName: ObjectName or ObjectName__c
CRITICAL: Standard objects use NO __c suffix: Case, Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity
ELEMENT ORDER inside <recordTypes> MUST be: 1. fullName 2. active 3. businessProcess (ONLY for Case/Lead/Opportunity/Solution — see below) 4. description (optional) 5. label 6. picklistValues (optional)
-- RECORD TYPE XML -- <recordTypes> <fullName>Record_Type_API_Name</fullName> <active>true</active> <description>Optional description</description> <label>Record Type Label</label> <picklistValues> <picklist>Status__c</picklist> <values> <fullName>Active</fullName> <default>false</default> </values> <values> <fullName>Inactive</fullName> <default>true</default> </values> </picklistValues> </recordTypes>
CRITICAL: Inside <values>, ONLY two elements allowed: <fullName> and <default> NEVER include <label> inside <values>.
== PROCESS-DRIVEN OBJECTS — CRITICAL == Case, Lead, Opportunity, and Solution record types REQUIRE a <businessProcess> element. Omitting it causes: "Required field is missing: businessProcess" Object → Business Process: Case→Support Process, Lead→Lead Process, Opportunity→Sales Process ALWAYS use the first entry from orgState.existingBusinessProcesses for the relevant object.
CORRECT XML for a Case record type: <recordTypes> <fullName>Technical_Support</fullName> <active>true</active> <businessProcess>Basic Support Process</businessProcess> <label>Technical Support</label> </recordTypes>
== CREATING A NEW BUSINESS PROCESS == The rule above ("use the first entry from orgState.existingBusinessProcesses") only applies when the ticket wants a record type on the object's DEFAULT/EXISTING process. If the ticket instead asks for a NEW, distinctly-named process (e.g. "create a new Lead Process called X", "a dedicated process for this record type") that process does not exist yet and MUST be generated as its own component — referencing it by name in <businessProcess> without also generating it deploys a record type whose businessProcess points at nothing, and fails with "no BusinessProcess named <Object>.<Name> found".
A BusinessProcess is embedded in the SAME CustomObject XML as the object's <recordTypes> blocks (same file, sibling elements — not a separate file): <CustomObject xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <businessProcesses> <fullName>New_Process_API_Name</fullName> <isActive>true</isActive> <values> <fullName>Opening_Status_Value</fullName> <default>true</default> </values> <values> <fullName>Another_Status_Value</fullName> <default>false</default> </values> <!-- one <values> block per status included in this process — exactly ONE of them must be <default>true</default>, see rule 5 below --> </businessProcesses> <recordTypes> <fullName>Record_Type_API_Name</fullName> <active>true</active> <businessProcess>New_Process_API_Name</businessProcess> <label>Record Type Label</label> </recordTypes> </CustomObject>
RULES for a new BusinessProcess (apply to any process-driven object, not just the one shown above): 1. Element order: fullName, description (optional), isActive, values — same <fullName>/<default>-only shape as <picklistValues><values> above; NEVER include <label> inside a businessProcess <values> block. 2. The record type's <businessProcess> value must be an EXACT match, character-for-character, of the new businessProcess's own <fullName> — this is the single most common point of failure. Generate both from one variable/value in your own reasoning so they can never drift apart. 3. Every <values><fullName> inside the businessProcess must be a status value that already exists on the object's status/stage picklist — either a standard value already in orgState, or a NEW value requested via an addStandardPicklistValues dmlOperation in this SAME response (see below). Never invent a value that isn't backed by an actual picklist entry somewhere in this deploy or the org. 4. This is a NEW component being created — it goes in the same CustomObject file as the object's other new pieces, it is never a reason to touch or restate any OTHER existing business process on the object. 5. DEFAULT VALUE RULE — CRITICAL: exactly ONE <values> entry inside the businessProcess must have <default>true</default> — every other entry must be <default>false</default>. Omitting this, or leaving every entry false, fails deploy with "No default value specified". This is normally whichever status represents the START of the process (e.g. the "Open"/"New"-style status), not the converted or closed one. Never leave two or more entries as default=true either — exactly one, always.
== ADDING NEW VALUES TO A STANDARD PICKLIST (Lead Status, Case Status, Opportunity Stage, Solution Status) == If a ticket asks to create NEW status/stage values that don't exist yet (e.g. "Create New Lead Status Values: Connected, Interested, ..."), do NOT hand-write a StandardValueSet XML file for this — that metadata type REPLACES the entire value list on deploy, and freehand-generating it risks silently dropping every existing value you don't know about, breaking the process for every other user of that object. Instead, emit a dmlOperations entry and let deterministic code merge it safely:
"dmlOperations": [ { "type": "addStandardPicklistValues", "objectApiName": "Lead", "fieldApiName": "Status", "newValues": ["Connected", "Interested", "Meeting Scheduled"] } ]
RULES: 1. Supported objectApiName.fieldApiName pairs: Lead.Status, Case.Status, Opportunity.StageName, Solution.Status. Do not use this op for any other picklist — custom fields' picklist values still go in that field's own <valueSet> inside its CustomField/embedded <fields> block as usual. 2. newValues is a list of the NEW value names ONLY — never list existing values, they are preserved automatically. Each entry may be a plain string (its label will match the value) or an object { "fullName": "...", "label": "..." } when the ticket wants a different display label. 3. Every new value referenced anywhere else in this response (a businessProcess, a record type's picklistValues, etc.) must appear in this newValues list — that is what makes the reference valid. 4. This entirely replaces any need to generate a StandardValueSet file yourself — never emit a files[] entry with metadataType StandardValueSet.
== STANDARD OBJECT RECORD TYPES — ABSOLUTE RULES == When the object is a STANDARD object: 1. MINIMAL CustomObject XML — ONLY <recordTypes> blocks inside <CustomObject>. NOTHING else. FORBIDDEN: <label>, <pluralLabel>, <nameField>, <sharingModel>, <deploymentStatus> 2. NEVER generate a CustomTab file for a standard object. 3. NEVER add <tabVisibilities> in any Profile XML for a standard object. 4. NEVER generate a Layout file for a standard object.
QUICK REFERENCE for standard-object record type (e.g. Account): File 1: objects/Account.object — CustomObject with ONLY <recordTypes> block(s) File 2: profiles/Admin.profile — Profile with <layoutAssignments> + <recordTypeVisibilities> NO CustomTab. NO <tabVisibilities>. NO Layout file. Ever.
-- PROFILE ASSIGNMENT FOR RECORD TYPES -- <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Profile xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <layoutAssignments> <layout>ObjectName-Layout Name</layout> <recordType>ObjectName.RecordTypeDeveloperName</recordType> </layoutAssignments> <recordTypeVisibilities> <recordType>ObjectName.RecordTypeDeveloperName</recordType> <default>false</default> <visible>true</visible> </recordTypeVisibilities> </Profile>
LAYOUT REFERENCE FORMAT: ObjectName-Layout Name (one dash). Example: Account-Account Layout HOW TO FIND STANDARD OBJECT LAYOUT NAME: use orgState.standardObjectLayoutNames["Account"][0]
DEFAULT RECORD TYPE RULE — CRITICAL: Salesforce requires exactly ONE recordTypeVisibility per object to have default=true. - If ticket says Default=true → set <default>true</default> - If ticket says Default=false but it is the only record type → STILL set <default>true</default> - NEVER emit <recordType>ObjectName.Master</recordType> — Master is not a valid Metadata API name - NEVER leave all recordTypeVisibilities with default=false
-- PICKLIST VALUES -- 1. Only include <picklistValues> if ticket specifies which values to assign 2. If ticket says "all values" → include ALL picklist values from existingFields in orgState 3. If ticket does not mention picklist values → OMIT <picklistValues> entirely 4. NEVER fabricate picklist values — only use values that exist in orgState
-- RULES SUMMARY -- 1. ALWAYS preserve ALL existing record types when updating — never drop any 2. For new object + record type → chained deployment 3. For existing object + record type → single deployment 4. NEVER emit two files[] entries with same filePath — merge into one
Record Type XML, Profile assignment, picklist values, process-driven objects
